additional_info.subject: SiD bkob1U failure
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
We have detected some issues with the Sicharge D charger bkob1U.
These are as follows:
When a vehicle is charging, occasionally one of the charger plugs becomes unavailable. This always happens when more than one vehicle is connected to the charger.
In the last few charging sessions, an attempt was made to stop the charge, but the Sicharge continued charging. The display shows "charging finished," but the process does not stop.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0456685-DC/Si-D/CL-[MP / R7 170002131] Charging Issue CRM:03057000042
additional_info.body:
Dear Lodhar,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0456685,
which was opened for charging issues on charger
bkob1U.
Apologies for the late reply
.
I analyzed the logs at the timestamps you provided, and these are my findings:
Outlet not in use going OoO
Timestamp: 2025-10-06​​​​​​​
DC2 and DC3 are charging
DC4 (outlet 5) goes out of order.
In the logs, I see an error on the SMC QA11-12, which is commanded to open, but the feedback was stuck to on. Because of this error on SMC, the Converter group of DC4 (outlet 5) is deactivated, as connected to multiple converter groups due to faulty SMC
The feedback of QA11-12 went to off only at 2025-10-06T16:58:28 (7 seconds later), but the outlet DC4 was already set as out of order.
I performed a research on AWS for the month of October, and saw that this error appeared 36 times in total. I would therefore suggest to replace the contactors QA11-12.
Stop charge not executed:
​​​​​​​Timestamp: 2025-10-16
​​​​​​​
I had a look at the logs, and the behavior of the charger is indeed unusual.
I see the SECC receiving a Stop, but this command is somehow not processed. At the same time, the charging goes on, but I do not see further logs regarding contactors and secc.
I Checked on AWS, and this behavior appeared other few times in October. For this reason, I will report the bug to R&D and wait for their instructions/analysis.
In order to provide R&D with a detailed summary, could you please tell me:
How was the session initially stopped when reached 80%? (From Backend, from EV, from HMI,..?)
How was the session eventually stopped, when it continued?
Thank you in advance for the valuable inputs!
On a side note, please be aware that the charger is currently registered as
out of warranty
in ISP.
Once I will receive your feedback, if you won't require any further support, I would proceed to close this ticket.
In case you require expert support, kindly create Work-order as per

afonso-sousa@siemens.com
or Teodoso, Rui (SI E CS SD ES) at
rui.teodoso@siemens.com
.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0456685-DC/Si-D/CL-[MP / R7 170002131] Charging Issue CRM:03057000042
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
After performing some tests by the client, it was detected that only one truck presented the issue of not ending the charging session when the instruction was given from the charger’s screen.
The client connected this truck to other chargers, obtaining the same result. It is believed that the problem is in the truck
How was the session initially stopped when reached 80%? (From Backend, from EV, from HMI,..?)
Answer:
When charging the trucks, the client sometimes tries to speed up the process by stopping the charge at 80%. This is always done from the charger’s screen by pressing
End Charging
.
How was the session eventually stopped, when it continued?
Answer:
The charging session ended automatically once it reached 100%.
